video_title: Wemby & Spurs On A REVENGE TOUR, NBA’s Most DOMINANT Team!

quotes.speaker: Michelle Beadle
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs are on a revenge tour following their NBA Finals loss
quotes.excerpt: I lived through them losing in 13 and then treating 14 as an entire just blinders on

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: I lived through them losing in 13 and then treating 14 as an entire just blinders on, get back to the finals and beat the Miami Heat. Does it feel like this Spurs squad is on one mission and one mission only?

text_blocks.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
text_blocks.text: I don't think they look at it as a crappy taste in their mouth at all. This is just a stepping stone forward. Their projection as far as becoming one of the greater teams in this league, I think they made an early jump and they had good results.

quotes.social_post: Michelle Beadle reflects on the Spurs mindset after their Finals loss, noting that for this squad, it is not about a bad taste in their mouth but rather a stepping stone toward becoming one of the greater teams in the league.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs are on a revenge tour after their Finals loss
quotes.excerpt: You can go in a training camp with a completely different mindset than anybody else around the league
quotes.quote: This is definitely a revenge tour. The most dangerous team that you can deal with is a young team that gets to the finals and they lose and you bring everybody back. You can go in a training camp with a completely different mindset than anybody else around the league because I got all the way there and I failed, but I still got everybody. Now when we come back into the season, we understand what it looks like to manage a schedule now. We understand our roles, we understand what it takes to get back into that position at the end of the season.
quotes.social_post: Lou Williams calls this a revenge tour for the Spurs. He argues that a young team returning with the same roster after a Finals loss has a completely different mindset and understands what it takes to manage a schedule and get back to that position.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs' Finals run was the best thing that could happen to them
quotes.excerpt: Looking back to that finals run, that could be the best thing that ever happened to them
quotes.quote: Looking back to that finals run, that could be the best thing that ever happened to them. For the players, for Wemby, for Castle, for Fox, for Mitch Johnson, for the entire organization to be that young and that talented and go to the finals and go up against a Knicks team that really was just on crazy momentum. It feels the opposite of them. They went to the NBA championship in the first time in 15 years, we're cool now. The Spurs look the exact opposite. They look like we are hungrier than ever, we are more determined, we know what it takes to get there.
quotes.social_post: Chandler Parsons believes the Spurs Finals run was the best thing that could happen to them. He says the team looks hungrier than ever and more determined to get back to the championship.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs are the most dominant team in the league right now
quotes.excerpt: From my eyes in 14 games, the San Antonio Spurs are the most dominant best team
quotes.quote: Not that they're lucky, but their OKC's banged up. That's not the team that we thought that was going to come in here. They're missing three starters for the rest of the season. So put them aside, I think San Antonio is the favorite to win it all. From my eyes in 14 games, the San Antonio Spurs are the most dominant best team in the league on both sides of the ball. And as good as Luka's been, I think he right now, if I had a vote, he would be the MVP, but the things that Wemby does on both sides of the ball, the block shots, the defense, that would possibly change my opinion.
quotes.social_post: Chandler Parsons says the San Antonio Spurs are the most dominant team in the league on both sides of the ball. He notes that while Luka is his current MVP pick, Wemby's defensive impact could change his opinion.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Philly has a deep core that can disrupt the Spurs
quotes.excerpt: I look at that Philly back court just as deep as as the Spurs
quotes.quote: The guys that I look at that can disrupt them is in the other conference. I look at that Philly back court just as deep as as the Spurs, but in the Western conference, I think they're catching a break right now because of the injuries that OKC has and Reeves kind of being in and out of the lineup in the Western conference. Other than that, they got it figured out. They showed us all last year that it wasn't a fluke. Dylan Harper is the real deal.
quotes.social_post: Lou Williams highlights the Philly backcourt as a team that could disrupt the Spurs, while noting that San Antonio is catching a break in the West due to injuries to the OKC roster.

quotes.speaker: Michelle Beadle
quotes.summary_phrase: Debating if Wembanyama or Luka should be the current MVP
quotes.excerpt: Do we sort of look at Luka like, well, I don't take him seriously that he's going to win

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: Wemby is averaging 30 points a game and he's playing just under 30 minutes a game. Do we sort of look at Luka like, well, I don't take him seriously that he's going to win a championship, but I do think he will win the MVP and maybe that's why we give him so much MVP love versus Wemby?

text_blocks.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
text_blocks.text: I believe so. Both guys are doing their thing this year and in different ways. Luka is absolutely dominating on the offensive side of the ball. Like I said earlier, this is something that we've only seen a handful of times in this league, so you have to give him his flowers for the offensive performance he's doing every night.

quotes.social_post: Michelle Beadle debates the MVP race between Wemby and Luka. She questions if we give Luka more MVP love because we doubt his championship chances, while acknowledging his offensive performance is something we have only seen a handful of times.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama is the foundation of a more talented Spurs team
quotes.excerpt: Wemby, I believe has a more talented team, but he's also the foundation of this group
quotes.quote: Wemby, I believe has a more talented team, but he's also the foundation of this group. So they're dominating in two different ways, but it has such a impact on their individual groups. It's honestly hard to determine. I feel like if you take Luka off that Lakers group, we don't have this many conversations about him. I feel like if you take Wemby off, there's still a solid group, but obviously not championship level.
quotes.social_post: DeMarcus Cousins weighs in on the MVP debate, suggesting that if you take Luka off the Lakers, the conversation changes, whereas Wemby is the foundation of a more talented Spurs group.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka's MVP case is helped by the Lakers' unexpected early success
quotes.excerpt: The biggest difference to me is that we expected the Spurs to be very good
quotes.quote: The biggest difference to me is that we expected the Spurs to be very good. They went to the finals, we know exactly who they are. It helps Luka that they're on this tear right now, that they're a top team in the Western conference. I didn't expect that. I knew the Spurs would be there. So the fact that Luka is now averaging 40, which he's going to have to stay around that number to out to out be Wemby for this award, that's just how it is.
quotes.social_post: Chandler Parsons says Luka's MVP case is helped by the Lakers unexpected early success. He notes that Luka will likely need to maintain a 40 point average to stay ahead of Wemby for the award.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: Anyone averaging 40 and 8 is the leader for MVP
quotes.excerpt: Anybody that's averaging 40 and 8 is the leader for the MVP right now
quotes.quote: Anybody that's averaging 40 and 8 is the leader for the MVP right now. Everything else you can cut the radio off. Guys that are averaging 40 and 8 and if he can stick around 35 plus throughout the season, it's not even a conversation. I don't care who they got as teammates.
quotes.social_post: DeMarcus Cousins is firm on the MVP race, stating that anyone averaging 40 and 8 is the leader for the award. He says if Luka can stay around 35 plus throughout the season, it is not even a conversation.
